newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey resumes farmer payments, still needs loans.
newsitem.headline: Turkey resumes farmer payments, still needs loans.

text.p: The Turkish Grain Board (TMO) has resumed payments to farmers after securing treasury funds for grain purchases, but still plans foreign borrowing, a senior farm official said.
The official said the TMO, whose purchases were interrupted two weeks ago, had recently obtained six trillion lira from the treasury to pay part of its debts to farmers.

"The TMO needs a bit more than 10 trillion lira to pay its debts to farmers from purchases so far. It obtained six trillion and therefore it needs another four or five trillion to complete payments for its purchases so far," the official told Reuters.
"We are planning foreign borrowing for that remaining amount," he said.
The TMO's urgently needs to borrow at least $60 million from international creditors. It has already lodged an application at the treasury for permission to borrow.
It borrowed $250 million via a syndicated loan last year to pay for grain purchases but used the money for this year's purchases as it bought very little from farmers last year.
The official said the TMO had so far bought 1.1 million tonnes of grain, at least 600,000 tonnes of that being barley and most of the rest durum wheat.
It plans to buy a total of 1.5 million tonnes of wheat and one million tonnes of barley in 1996/97, for which it needs some 40 trillion lira in total including its payments so far.
